new_scholarship.description: The MAEC-AECID programme family (Becas Cooperación Española) is run by the Spanish Agency for International Development Cooperation (AECID) and funds training for Spanish citizens and for citizens of Spanish-cooperation partner countries, both in Spain and abroad. The official page groups the live 2026/2027 calls into four blocks: scholarships for young Spaniards, readerships (Lectorados) for Spaniards teaching Spanish abroad, scholarships for citizens of Latin America, Africa and Asia, and artistic or research residencies at the Real Academia de España en Roma. As of 2026-10-04 every 2026/2027 sub-programme listed on the official pages is marked "Plazo cerrado", so the next cycle is upcoming. Awards are financial support (a monthly stipend plus, for some programmes, Social Security registration or health insurance); the official pages reviewed do not state that tuition fees are paid.

programme_detail_official.description: AECID's Becas Cooperación Española (MAEC-AECID) is the Spanish government's scholarship family for training Spanish citizens and citizens of partner countries, delivered in Spain and overseas. The official scholarship section groups the live calls into scholarships for young Spaniards, Lectorados for Spaniards, scholarships for citizens of Latin America, Africa and Asia, and residencies at the Real Academia de España en Roma. Support is financial: a monthly stipend plus, in several programmes, Social Security registration or health and accident insurance. All 2026/2027 sub-programmes were closed when checked on 2026-10-04.

application_readiness_checklist: Identify the exact sub-programme first: this umbrella row covers programmes with different eligibility, dates and budgets
Read the Convocatoria text and annexes for your sub-programme on the AECID Electronic Office before applying
Check the Anexo list of available destinations (e.g. Anexo I for Programa COOPERACIÓN, Anexo II for Programa CULT) for the places you can apply to
Have your admission or pre-admission paperwork ready where the Convocatoria requires it
Register and access the AECID Electronic Office (www.aecid.gob.es) in advance
If you are a public employee in a programme-required country, obtain your hierarchical authorisation before applying
common_rejection_risks: Applying to the umbrella record in general instead of a named sub-programme with its own eligibility rules
Missing the 10-business-day window counted from BOE publication, which is short and programme-specific
Applying for a Lectorados post without the required university degree, Spanish-teaching experience or under-37 status
Failing the age ceiling in the relevant Convocatoria
Not holding the citizenship the sub-programme is restricted to (for example, non-Spanish applicants cannot use the Becas para jóvenes españoles programmes)
Not holding admission to the target master's by the time the application is submitted, which the África-Med programme explicitly requires
estimated_uncovered_costs: The official pages reviewed do not state a monthly amount, so budget for the gap between the unpublished stipend and living costs in Madrid or the host city
Travel costs to and from Spain are not described in the pages reviewed
Any tuition or enrolment fees at the host institution, which the official pages do not commit to covering
Costs of documents, translations and legalisation required by the Convocatoria
document_audit: Electronic application submitted through the Sede electrónica AECID before 23:59:59 Madrid time on the closing date
Full Convocatoria text and the relevant annexes downloaded and checked against your programme
Proof of citizenship or nationality for the restricted-citizenship programmes

Admission or pre-admission confirmation from the host institution or programme
Authorisation from your employing body where the Convocatoria requires it
Copy of any prior AECID non-beneficiary certificate requested by the Electronic Office
